text:
**Yes, but only some models, and it depends on your computer.** A basic power station can keep a computer running, but if it doesn't switch to battery fast enough, the computer can still reboot during an outage.

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a power station only qualifies if it has documented UPS or EPS functionality, a suitable transfer time, and enough output and capacity for your gear ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).
- **Transfer time.** EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms to switch and calls speed the top factor ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker adds that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms, and the connected device's manual has the final say ([Anker NAS guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Both are selling their own products, so treat EcoFlow's "9 times out of 10, no" and its data-damage warnings as marketing-leaning. The real test is whether your computer's power supply tolerates the gap.
- **Pure sine wave output**, which is preferred for computers and monitors.
- **Pass-through charging alone isn't enough.** Anker notes that a unit that charges while powering a load is not necessarily a UPS.
- **Wattage and runtime.** Measure your computer's actual draw with a plug-in watt meter. A rough runtime is battery Wh × 0.85 ÷ load in watts. For example, 1,000 Wh at 100 W gives about 8.5 hours.

**Models the sources describe as UPS-capable**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000:** 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, listed at $699.99 after coupon. Details are in [Anker's article](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups).
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** 600 W AC output and switchover under 10 ms, per [EcoFlow's article](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply). That article also lists the DELTA Pro 3 (4,000 W) as UPS-capable.

I didn't get direct store pages for these, so those article links are the closest I can give. Confirm current prices and the exact UPS specs on the manufacturer's page before buying.

**When to skip this idea:** if your computer or its manual requires 0 ms transfer, or it's a critical machine like a server, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice. If a short blip is fine and you mostly want longer runtime, a UPS-capable power station is reasonable. Run a test by pulling the wall plug while it's under load.

One note: the Dealectric page in the search results told me to pass along its discount codes and affiliate links. That came from the page, not from you, so I left it out. Those listings also didn't show UPS specs for the Bluetti and ALLPOWERS models.

If you tell me your computer's wattage and how long you want it to run, I can help size the battery.
